ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZVPYmA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhC8geU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 31, "title": "Preserve 8237 address, count and mode registers across master clear", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `beb4c7d3a5286738a2c29c11855773881e70dc14`, writing PC-98 DMA master-clear port `001Bh` replaces the entire `Dma` object with `Default`, then masks all channels. This destroys programmed current/base addresses, counts and modes. Guest software cannot resume using retained channel programming after unmasking. See [Dma::write](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/beb4c7d3a5286738a2c29c11855773881e70dc14/src/devices.rs#L268).

This handler predates completed Issue #29/PR #30. Their terminal-count auto-init improvement does not fix or test master-clear retention. The supplied context lists no open Issues.

## Expected outcome

Implement the documented software-reset behavior for the currently modeled 8237 core state:

- Any byte written to master clear clears status and the shared first/last byte pointer, sets all four channel masks, and leaves the controller idle.
- Preserve each channel’s current and base address/count registers and mode. Master clear must neither reload bases nor zero channel programming.

Intel specifies that master clear clears Command, Status, Request, Temporary and First/Last Flip-Flop registers and sets Mask. Retention of address/count/mode follows from this selective reset definition; these registers are absent from its reset list. See [Intel 8237A datasheet, printed pp. 2 and 9, including Figure 6](https://read.seas.harvard.edu/~kohler/class/04f-aos/ref/hardware/8237A.pdf#page=9). NEC identifies PC-9801 master clear at `1Bh` and byte-pointer clear at `19h` in [application note IEA-751, §2.4, Table 2-10, printed p. 15](https://www.renesas.com/ja/document/apn/upd72070-application-note#page=30).

Scope is software master clear between device services and its existing FDC consumer. Do not add software requests, command-register functionality, memory-to-memory transfers or arbitration. Command/Request/Temporary state is currently unmodeled and remains a disclosed gap. Keep existing machine construction/reset and external PC-98 bank-register policy unchanged; board-level bank-reset wiring is outside this Issue and remains unverified.

## Context and reproduction

A focused native reproduction using public `Dma` methods:

1. Program channel 2 address `2340h`, count `0003h`, and auto-init mode `56h`, using the existing byte-pointer protocol.
2. Service one byte with `advance(2)`, obtaining current address/count `2341h/0002h`, distinct from the saved bases.
3. Write any byte to port `1Bh`.
4. Read current registers. Present code returns zero; expected values remain `2341h/0002h`. Later service after unmasking must still use the saved programming.

[tests/dma.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/beb4c7d3a5286738a2c29c11855773881e70dc14/tests/dma.rs) already covers terminal count, partial programming, shared byte sequencing and consecutive raw FDC transfers, but has no master-clear retention assertion. Its `read_word` helper explicitly clears the pointer, so it cannot independently prove master clear resets that pointer.

Project progress: #29/#30 completed the bounded terminal-count/auto-init behavior. The Coordinator reports 105 native integration tests and 48 Chromium/Wasm tests passing, with alternate browser ports after a server-port conflict; see [recorded validation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/beb4c7d3a5286738a2c29c11855773881e70dc14/docs/validation.md#issue-29-dma-terminal-count-auto-init). These results were not rerun by this evaluator. DMA and integration remain partial; every other supplied inventory category, status and required scope remains unchanged.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replace destructive core-register initialization in the master-clear handler with the bounded behavior above, without unrelated refactoring.
- [ ] Add original native regressions covering all four channels, increment/decrement, auto-init enabled/disabled, and current values distinct from bases. Verify retained programming through public readback and subsequent service; prove saved bases through eventual auto-init reload.
- [ ] Exercise both initial byte-pointer phases, latched terminal-count status, mixed channel masks, repeated clears, and data bytes `00h`, `55h`, `FFh`. Check the first register access immediately after master clear without an intervening `19h` write. Check partial-byte programming survives the command.
- [ ] On VM and Ap, add raw-port FDC integration cases for reads and writes: program DMA in bank zero, master-clear, verify a masked command transfers no bytes or disk data, then unmask without rewriting address/count/mode and verify successful transfer. Assert exact data and guards, expected result bytes, completion IRQ and subsequent command readiness. Preserve existing auto-init and stale-status regressions.
- [ ] Extend the existing original MIT DMA boot probe with a focused master-clear phase while retaining its existing assertions. Check retained readback and successful raw FDC read/write after unmasking, with bounded waits and an explicit master-clear PASS/FAIL result. Execute the same source-built probe natively and in production Wasm on both profiles at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Record reproducible assembly command, license, source/image hashes and execution budget; update only the affected DMA fixture manifest intentionally. No commercial ROM or guest software is required.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the new focused native regression and guest phase fail against baseline `beb4c7d3a5286738a2c29c11855773881e70dc14` and pass with the fix.
- [ ] The Coordinator performs the [README fixture preparation and checks](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/beb4c7d3a5286738a2c29c11855773881e70dc14/README.md#reproduce-the-checks), including `cargo test --locked --test dma`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `python3 tools/build_media.py --check`, `python3 tools/build_font.py --check`, and `npm test`. Preserve existing hardware, DOS/application, VM and game regressions and assertions. Report actual results and any failures; do not silently skip missing licensed fixtures.
- [ ] Document the bounded contract and evidence. DMA remains partial: software requests, command controls, verify transfers, demand/block/single arbitration, external EOP, memory-to-memory, cascade/rotating priority, bank-reset fidelity and broader device interactions remain incomplete or unverified. Limited probe success establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility. No other inventory category loses scope or gains an unsupported verification claim.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
